days.subject: Day 1 of 7: let's fix how you sit
days.preview: Four small alignment checks that make everything else work.
days.title: Your sitting foundation
days.intro: Welcome to your 7-Day Reset. Over the next week you'll get one short, practical step each morning. Today is the base everything else builds on: how you actually sit.
steps: Feet flat on the floor
Not crossed, not tucked under the chair.
Hips all the way back
Sit on your sit bones, not your tailbone.
Shoulders back and down
Away from your ears, relaxed rather than pulled.
Ears over shoulders
Think tall, not stiff.
days.tip: Try the four checks now, while you read this. Then once more after lunch.
days.reply_prompt: Quick question: where do you feel it most after a long sit? Lower back, neck, or hips? Just hit reply. We read every message.
days.tomorrow: Tomorrow: setting up your cushion and lumbar support so good posture takes less effort.

days.subject: Day 2 of 7: set up your support in 3 minutes
days.preview: Where your cushion and lumbar support should actually sit.
days.title: Setting up your support
days.intro: Yesterday you set your alignment. Today we add the support layer, so holding that position stops feeling like work.
steps: Place the seat cushion at the back
Push it right into the back of the seat so your tailbone sits in the cut-out.
Set the lumbar support at belt height
It should meet the natural curve of your lower back.
Lean back and let it work
The support holds your spine so your muscles can relax.
days.tip: If it feels odd for the first hour, that's normal. Your body is getting used to sitting upright again.
days.reply_prompt: Not sure you've got the position right? Reply with a photo of your chair setup and we'll check it for you.
days.tomorrow: Tomorrow: your screen, desk and keyboard.

days.subject: Day 3 of 7: your screen, desk and keyboard
days.preview: Small workspace tweaks that stop you leaning forward.
days.title: Screen, desk and keyboard setup
days.intro: Your workspace either supports your posture or pulls you out of it. Today's tweaks take five minutes and stop the forward lean that undoes your setup.
steps: Screen at arm's length
The top of the screen at, or just below, eye level.
Chair height for 90° elbows
Hands rest on the keyboard with elbows bent at about a right angle.
Keyboard and mouse close
Wrists neutral, mouse right next to the keyboard.
days.tip: On a laptop? A stack of books under it plus a cheap external keyboard makes a big difference.
days.reply_prompt: Working from a laptop, a sofa or a kitchen table? Reply and tell us. We'll send a tip for your setup.

days.subject: Day 4 of 7: breaking the slouch habit
days.preview: The 20-second reset that keeps you upright all day.
days.title: Breaking the slouch habit
days.intro: Your setup is done. Now for the part that makes it last: small, regular resets so slouching never gets the chance to settle in.
steps: The 20/20 reset
Every 20 minutes, take 20 seconds to re-check your posture.
Reset in three moves
Sit tall, roll your shoulders back and down, tuck your chin slightly.
Get up every 90 minutes
Stand, stretch, walk, grab water. Movement is medicine.
days.tip: Set a silent 20-minute repeating timer on your phone or watch for the next two days. After that it starts to become automatic.
days.reply_prompt: Halfway there. On a scale of 1 to 10, how does sitting feel compared with Day 1? Reply with a number.
days.tomorrow: Tomorrow: simple movement to release tension.

days.subject: Day 5 of 7: move better, feel better
days.preview: Three easy movements to release desk tension.
days.title: Move better, feel better
days.intro: Even perfect posture gets stiff if you hold it all day. Today is about adding small amounts of movement through your day.
steps: Stand 2 to 3 minutes every hour
Phone calls are a great time to stand.
Add simple stretches
Neck rolls, shoulder rolls and a gentle back stretch.
Hydrate and breathe
Drink water, take a few slow, deep breaths. Awareness is half the work.
days.tip: Your cushion and lumbar support keep you aligned when you sit back down, so movement and support work together.
days.reply_prompt: Which stretch felt best? Reply and let us know. It helps us improve the program.
days.tomorrow: Tomorrow: building the strength to hold good posture.

days.subject: Day 6 of 7: build strength, not strain
days.preview: Gentle core and back work so good posture lasts.
days.title: Build strength, not strain
days.intro: Good posture isn't only about sitting right. It's about having the strength to stay that way without thinking about it.
steps: Gently engage your core
Like zipping up a fitted pair of jeans. Relaxed, not rigid.
Strengthen your upper back
Shoulder-blade squeezes and chest openers counter long hours at a desk.
Build gradually
A few minutes a day beats one big session. Consistency over intensity.
days.tip: Do 10 shoulder-blade squeezes every time you refill your water. That's your whole workout.
days.reply_prompt: Any exercise you'd like us to explain in more detail? Just reply.
days.tomorrow: Tomorrow: the last day, and how to keep it going.

days.subject: Day 7 of 7: you did it. Here's how to keep it going
days.preview: The four habits that make this week stick.
days.title: Reset, recover and keep it going
days.intro: You've built the foundation, set up your support and started new habits. That's a real change. Today is about making it stick.
steps: Keep your posture resets
The 20/20 check is the single most useful habit from this week.
Recover with movement
Walk, stretch or do light strength work most days.
Listen to your body
Discomfort is a signal, not a failure. Adjust and reset.
Let your support do the work
Your cushion and lumbar support keep you aligned every day.
days.tip: Bookmark the 7-Day Reset page. Run through it again any time things start to slip.
days.reply_prompt: We'd love to hear how your week went. Reply with one thing that changed for you. It genuinely makes our day.
